> **Status: Current planning checklist; no release candidate exists.**
> Product baseline: `7edddbdb8e8512627aed0ed42533ef099d802384`.
> This issue tracks implementation and owning contract proofs. Creating it does not claim implementation, benchmark qualification, merge approval or resolution of the related tickets.

## Goal and relationship

Implement bounded-memory live Workspace state and full Commit, with incremental selected generations, concurrent arbitrary commands and multiple Workspaces. Filesystem mutations enter through ordinary supported kernel/FUSE operations independently of how an authorized process was launched. Keep canonical processing/publication and the SQLite Store in the Server.

Benchmark and qualification companion: **[#288](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/288)**.

Primary related scopes: #245, #248, #256, #249, #219, #259 and #261. Deferred traceability remains in #276, with separate observer/canary obligations under #283/#235. Keep #276 as the owner's single deferred ledger; do not close it or split away unfinished rows.

## Design handoff and first publication checkpoint

The complete researched packet is currently a task-owned local draft, not a published GitHub tree:

`/Users/yifanxu/.codex/worktrees/issue286-phase-b/layerfs/core/docs/architecture/proposal/bounded-workspace-implementation-20260930/`

It contains `README.md`, `LAYOUT.md`, `WORKSPACE.md`, `SERVER.md`, `CONCURRENCY.md`, `ACCEPTANCE.md`, `ISSUE276-AND-SCALING.md`, `ROLLOUT.md`, `ISSUE-CLOSURE.md`, `EVALUATION.md` and source/LOC captures. The local `scenarios.md` adds SC01–08, and `benchmark_agent_report.md` contains report requirements.

**R0 publishes the full packet and scenarios at a source-pinned repository commit and links them here before implementation starts.** Preserve unrelated output and other owners' worktrees. Do not invent blob links to unpublished files. The acceptance below makes this ticket independently reviewable while that publication is pending.

Published workload context: [#245 load-bearing cases](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d63379b955d1af4656cbfe23ebefc05ebf36ef8c/core/docs/issues/245/LOAD_BEARING_CASES.md). Its old implementation limits remain historical.

## Selected architecture and invariants

### 1. Paged live authority and final-state overwrite

- Private v3 uses per-file persistent interval roots plus paged inode/name/parent/dirty/saved/orphan/payload-location/owner/cleanup facts.
- Each accepted syscall publishes one coherent selected revision. Overlapping writes replace covered logical ranges and share untouched subtrees. They do not create a recursively traversed old-file-version chain for every WRITE.
- Commit consumes surviving final state, not a journal of every prior command/write. Real accepted input, fragmentation and cleanup work remain charged.
- Split/join cuts bounded boundary paths. Wide overwrite/truncate carries removed subtree roots to bounded cleanup rather than collecting all affected intervals in RAM.
- A per-inode mutation lease orders conflicting writes; a namespace-ordering lease plus sorted affected inode leases orders multi-key namespace mutations. Prepare large candidates outside global publication locks, then apply bounded key/path changes to the **current** catalog.
- Handles, directory cursors/cookies, selected roots and caches are admitted by actual owner resources or explicitly selected supported policy; no hidden fixed handle/cookie/root/session cap may undercut the #256/#249 profile. Listing/frame batches do not cap total directory size.

### 2. Exact generations, streaming and READY

- Capture selects immutable G1 and opens G2 over G1's complete effective view, including names, creates, moves, tombstones and orphan facts.
- First touch in each successor generation starts with one opaque span of the exact predecessor file. Lowering stops at inherited spans; it must not repeatedly enumerate historical predecessor fragmentation.
- Keep immutable selected source/location contexts and precise pins. Known saved results bind the predecessor to its proved canonical result; no stale-ancestor substitution or recursive exception-resolver chain.
- Unified FileSet/binding cursors cover one/many/large files. Initial FileSet units are bounded by at most512 members and4MiB encoded target, with the same grammar/assembler for a large singleton.
- Fresh input streams directly into private C2 construction with exact EOF; inherited changed input has one required quota-owned replay source. Fixed windows do not excuse unbounded file-cache residency.
- Results use bounded data frames into paged saved facts and one unit completion seal. Losing a terminal retains exact Unknown custody; no group resend.
- READY protects saved/exception/outcome/install/failure/cleanup resources before the **single composite namespace + HistoryCommit request**. The Server pre-admits successor validity/terminal authority before Branch CAS.
- Known-result install preserves the actual current G2 and changes fixed selection/baseline facts. No proportional reconciliation allocation remains after publication. Public Commit includes its required cleanup.

### 3. Canonical locality and physical storage

- C1 stays pure logical construction/verification with narrow injected object/state/finalized-consumer boundaries. C2 owns codecs/packs/SQLite/scratch; C5 owns history/allocation/expected-head publication.
- Selected end-state is immediate-parent file-edit policy v2, versioned FileState policy identity, and namespace profile v2 with an authenticated parent tree.
- Hash authentication alone is not semantic namespace certification. Initial/import/unproven-root certification proves full correspondence/cycles; incremental successor validation uses checked changed effects and affected ancestor paths.
- NamespaceValidityLease binds principal/issuer epoch/root/profile/scope and live owners. No recursive proof-history DAG or unlimited historical-root registry.
- Independently qualify v2 roots/partitions; preserve exact retained v1 compatibility separately. Equal logical bytes do not imply equal versioned IDs.
- C2 schema11 admits new parent roles beyond schema10's1–13. Existing Store migration requires proven deployment-wide quiescence, bounded indexed metadata copy/equality checks, a small schema transition and bounded retired-row cleanup. Preserve pack payloads/save IDs/ordinals and account physical freelist/high-water.
- Import a selected v1 snapshot into a **new v2 Stack/scope**, using paged serial remap and existing C5 initialization. No silent in-place profile conversion, automatic migration/recovery or guessed Unknown continuation.

### 4. Memory, admission and retirement

- Resident working sets are admitted windows/cursors/caches; growing populations are quota-owned paged facts. Account encoded/decoded/clone/draft/engine/result overlap.
- Keep C2 Save capacity unchanged, initially2. Separate short C5 catalog admission with protected executor/control/FD/byte/engine headroom. Inode refill must progress while both bulk Save slots are occupied.
- Each admitted Commit leases its working set from the shared envelope. Idle Workspaces do not reserve full Commit buffers. Protected completion capacity cannot be consumed by G2 or another Workspace.
- Heap, SQLite, daemon, child, file cache, kernel/socket/dirty/writeback and temporary disk have explicit domains. The proposed standard Server profile is176MiB first-party +32MiB SQLite +16MiB fixed +32MiB cache/kernel =256MiB; these are proposed admission numbers, not measured PASS.
- Strict physical Server containment is a separate supported native-Linux cgroup capability. Logical semantics remain host-independent; unsupported required enforcement returns Unsupported. Do not silently alter benchmark hosting.
- Paged reference edges and cleanup jobs reclaim only after exact last-owner/native-identity/block checks. Pins/Unknown owners and cleanup backlog stay charged. No guessed refund, population-sized cleanup list or lock-held recursive destruction.

### 5. Command and mount ownership

- Generic public WorkspaceApi::exec accepts arbitrary command bytes. No command/executable/workload classifier, special benchmark mutation route or automatic range-splice recognition.
- Authorized external processes with mount visibility and the correct actor use the same supported FUSE mutation path. External process supervision is separately owned; filesystem capture does not automatically give LayerFS custody of that process.
- Replace the whole-command30s cap end to end with negotiated UntilOwnedExit and exact start/wait/cancel ownership. Keep finite connect/admission/stalled-I/O/callback/Commit/cleanup bounds, bounded output and at most one unsent liveness event.
- Owned event-driven I/O/supervision replaces per-Exec helper stacks and cumulative command/PID/timer scans. Treat leader exit, domain empty, reaping, pipe completion and terminal delivery separately.
- Key the registry by Workspace ID+incarnation. Operator max_workspaces_per_sandbox counts attaching/live/closing/retained owners exactly once; default2 is a policy value, not an architectural maximum. Prove configured1/2/3.
- One pending Commit per Workspace; different Workspaces may Commit when resources admit them. Shared-Branch HeadMoved is explicit, with no merge/rebase/retry.
- RuntimeActor and privileged BackingOwner are separate. Prove mount/actor/issued-handle authorization, bootstrap/domain membership before user code, no inherited control authority and exact descendant cleanup.
- Own a first-party cancellable Linux FUSE session with independent interrupt ingress and single-use RequestLease replies. An EINTR accepted before publication cannot be followed by candidate publication; already accepted publication keeps its actual result.
- Truthful statfs, precise daemon-death mount recovery and explicit dirty-discard are separate workflows. Exit7/cancel/disconnect preserves accepted writes. Unknown submission forbids guessed discard. Unmount is detachment.

## Rollout and dependency checkpoints

- [ ] **R0 — Publish and freeze:** full packet/scenarios, record/schema/wire/capability/opcode contracts, independent v1/v2 oracle sources, simultaneous-window arithmetic, runtime/migration authority and exact supported profiles.
- [ ] **R1 — Resource foundation:** paged state ports, ordered runs/indexes/cursors, admitted caches, typed C2/C5 permits and protected completion/control capacity. Prove progress/refusal before dependent effects.
- [ ] **R2 — Workspace v3:** live split/join/current publisher, source contexts, paged authority, exact conflict leases and bounded retirement. Prove ordinary syscall semantics and unrelated-inode progress.
- [ ] **R3 — Server construction:** FileSet/binding/result streaming, exact external C1 state, canonical v2 certification/policy, schema11 migration/import implementation and Unknown custody.
- [ ] **R4 — Full Commit:** smallest complete mutation→capture→construction→Branch→install→cleanup slice, then file/namespace/G1/G2/pin/failure/resource gates. Include #248 >65,535 runs and #256 handle/listing/count/wide-rebind obligations.
- [ ] **R5 — Native runtime:** FUSE interruption/identity/quota/death/discard and owned long-command/channel/domain lifecycle, including authorized external mounted-path writers.
- [ ] **R6 — Concurrent enablement:** #249/#219 after #248 prerequisites; same-W and cross-W progress, independent submissions, exact conflicts, admission and retained-owner isolation.
- [ ] **R7 — Cutover/retirement:** explicit Store/snapshot transitions, old-owner drain and deletion of displaced mutable authority. Preserve required v1 readers/contracts, exact Unknown custody and versioned support boundaries.

Workspace, Server/storage and runtime/transport can be developed against the shared contracts in parallel; Bridge changes have one coordinated owner. Design concurrency early; enable it only after its prerequisite composition passes. Do not automatically advance/cherry-pick other unmerged candidates.

## Module, source-size and engineering rules

Follow the existing Core crate boundaries and SRP ownership: Workspace backing/active/{nodes,files,catalog,generations,payloads,custody} and commit/{prepare,files,namespace,results,ready,install,completion}; daemon workspaces/commands/control/transport/platform; FUSE projection/linux session; C1 file/filesystem; C2 construction_state/sqlite/migration.

- Product-only src; external tests; production files<=999 physical lines and lib.rs/mod.rs<=200 declaration/delegation lines.
- No universal manager/plugin/runtime framework, empty scaffolding or first-party implementation hidden outside the production scope.
- No third-party patches/forks/vendors, new dependency when existing capability suffices, automatic retry/fallback, WAL/sync/crash-durability expansion or added construction workers.
- Preserve one producer per construction operation and actual quotas. Larger logical/body/count profiles need separate review and qualification.
- **Never trade approximately5% storage saving for approximately50% speed loss.** The owner's5%-for-5% example is acceptable; existing history allocation tolerance is up to10%, not unbounded temporary storage.
- Record exact per-commit first-parent/final staged/committed production LOC, reference/Core/combined and the same reproducible method. Baseline: reference65,417; Core70,279; combined135,696. Net +5,500..+26,500 is a broad researched forecast, not an implementation budget. Retire displaced authority when safe and report temporary duplication honestly.
- Update affected architecture and source pins with the owning source change. Run owning locked Core tests/examples/fmt/Clippy and boundary/self-tests at coherent final handoff; no CI or retired aggregate preflight.

## Completion and scope boundaries

Implementation completion requires the documented supported profile, independent state/root/failure proofs and owning checks. Companion benchmark qualification remains distinct. Targeted closures are #248/#256/#249/#219/#259, then #261/#245 only with their complete acceptance. #276/#283/#235/#174 keep remaining ledger/proof requirements; do not blanket-close tickets.

SC01–08 cover frequent/overlapping edits, sparse and dense large-file changes, many tiny files, namespace moves/removal, G1/G2 overlap, pins/failure/output/admission and multi-command/multi-Workspace load. Larger tiers are not automatically supported. The10,240 case remains owner-deferred until selected. Writable mmap, complete DB locking/crash durability, S3 storage, conflict resolution and stronger sibling filesystem confinement remain separate capabilities.
title: Phase 5: implement bounded streaming Commit and concurrent Workspaces
